title: Welsh Cakes
subtitle: Traditional Welsh griddle cakes with currants
excerpt: Small, flat, scone-like cakes cooked on a griddle or dry frying pan, spiced with mixed spice and stuffed with currants. Eaten warm, dusted with caster sugar. The national cake of Wales.

recipe.sourceNotes: Welsh cakes (pice ar y maen, literally 'cakes on the stone') are a traditional Welsh baked good cooked on a bakestone (a flat iron griddle) over an open fire or range, a method that predates the widespread availability of ovens in Welsh homes. The bakestone was a central piece of domestic equipment in Welsh rural households, and many traditional Welsh baked goods — Welsh cakes, crempog (Welsh pancakes), and teisen lap (moist Welsh cake) — were cooked on it rather than in an oven. Welsh cakes are midway in texture between a scone and a biscuit: they have a shortbread-like crumb from the rubbed-in fat, but are risen slightly and remain soft inside. They are best eaten warm from the griddle, dusted with caster sugar. They keep for a few days in a tin but are best fresh.

recipeTools.notes: A flat griddle or heavy frying pan. A round 7 cm pastry cutter.

content.text: The griddle must be heated to a moderate temperature before cooking: too hot and the outside chars before the inside cooks through; too cool and the cakes dry out without colouring. A medium-low heat is correct: the cakes should take about 3 minutes per side. The dough is handled like shortcrust: rubbed fat produces a crumb texture. Do not overwork the dough. Roll to about 7 mm thick: thinner and the cakes dry out; thicker and they will be raw in the centre.

Sift the flour, baking powder, mixed spice, and salt into a bowl. Rub in the cold butter until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs. Stir in the sugar and currants. Add the beaten egg and mix to a soft but not sticky dough, adding a little milk if needed.
Roll out on a lightly floured board to about 7 mm thick. Cut into rounds with a 7 cm cutter. Re-roll the trimmings.

Heat a dry, heavy frying pan or griddle over medium-low heat. Cook the Welsh cakes in batches for 3 minutes each side until golden-brown and cooked through. They should feel dry to the touch in the centre. Dust immediately with caster sugar. Eat warm.
